## Brand Strategy
- Positioning: "The heart and soul of football."
- Goal: re-establish Umbro as one of the most important names in football, approaching 90th anniversary.
- Unified look and feel across every aspect of the business, every country, every level of the game.
- Brand promise: quality, insight, great design delivered with style.
- Football-metaphor-driven communication: guidelines likened to a "great football manager."
- Centralized governance: Global Brand Marketing Team approval required for exceptions.

## Logo
- "Stacked double diamond" -- the iconic Umbro mark.
- Primary use: black (Pantone Black, CMYK 0/0/0/100).
- Secondary: white-out version for dark/complex backgrounds (not a boxed logo).
- Clearance area defined by the height of the inner diamond (used as measurement unit for clearance zone).
- Minimum print size: 13mm wide x 8.5mm high.
- Minimum web size: 79px wide x 51px high.
- Exceptional color changes permitted only with Global Brand Marketing Team approval (for team/sponsor harmonization).

## Color
- Primary: Pantone Black.
- White for reversed applications.
- Partner-specific color exceptions allowed with approval.

## Graphics
- Heritage patterns: iconic historical Umbro designs used on business card reverses (6 pattern variants: A-F).
- Patterns drawn from "Umbro's rich history" -- heritage as a design asset.

- Not captured in sampled pages.

## Applications
- Business cards: 85x55mm, Pantone Black front, CMYK reverse. Stock: GFSmith Lettra 100% Cotton Ultrawhite 300gsm.
- Letterheads: heritage pattern on reverse, licensee text requirements specified.
- Licensee guidelines: required disclaimer text with specific positioning (bottom left corner).
- Covers "signage to shin pads" per introduction.

## Tone of Voice
- Enthusiastic, football-passionate, colloquial British tone.
- Motivational and inclusive ("With your help...").
- Heritage-proud but forward-looking.
- Practical, directive, approachable.

## Outliers
- Compact 38 pages -- efficient for a sportswear brand covering product, communications, and retail.
- Strong licensee governance framework: specific text requirements, approval processes.
- Heritage patterns as a design system element is distinctive -- turns brand history into a modular graphic asset.
- Named contact person (Helene Hope, Head of Global Brand Operations) -- personal accountability.
- Iconix Brand UK Ltd ownership context (corporate parent referenced in stationery).

## Quality Score
**3/5** -- Solid, practical brand guide with clear logo rules and good application detail. The heritage-pattern system is a nice touch. However, the sampled pages suggest limited strategic depth compared to larger guides, and the document is relatively compact. Good for operational use but not a design-thinking benchmark.
